scope: Structural and JLPTEI-3 guideline audit of physical scans 96–109 (printed pp. 34–41). Covered the HE (prayerbook_for_the_new_year-heidenheim-1965-he) and EN (prayerbook_for_the_new_year-marmorstein-1965-en) bodies and standOff in /tmp/mahzor-backlog/s96-109-current-xml.xml, both current-readings.json dossiers, the human decisions file human_morning_s96_s109_snippets_1_to_5.json, and the morning sequence in machzor_expanded-opensiddur-he/index.xml lines 1480–1529. This does not accept source wording, fine marks or citation wording.

findings.location: Bundle line 23 (HE): j:conditional xml:id="el_adon_segment_2" with its note "אַם שַׁבָּת.", up to j:endConditional target="#el_adon_segment_2" before stanza 3. Bundle line 325 (EN): the same id with note "On Sabbath.", inserted between "merit and equity are" and "before His throne".
findings.problem: This nested conditional repeats the whole poem's own condition (el_adon_condition, shabbat=true), so it adds no liturgical meaning. The printed "אם שבת" here is a running marker at the top of p. 38 for the Shabbat layer, not a condition on one couplet. Encoding it as a conditional causes three problems. (1) When Shabbat is undefined, the instruction and a closing delimiter print in the middle of stanza el_adon/2. (2) The HE and EN scopes differ: HE covers the whole couplet זכות…כבודו, while EN starts mid-sentence and leaves "merit and equity are" outside. (3) It suggests that only this line depends on Shabbat.
findings.fix: Delete the el_adon_segment_2 j:conditional, including its tei:note, and its j:endConditional in both files. Keep the tei:pb n="38" exactly where it is. If the top-of-page marker must be kept, record it in the source README or dossier as page furniture, not as a condition.

findings.problem: The quotation covers only בָּרוּךְ כְּבוֹד־ה׳ מִמְּקוֹמוֹ, which is the part of Ezekiel 3:12 after the etnachta on גָּדוֹל. A whole-verse source claims וַתִּשָּׂאֵנִי רוּחַ… as well, which is not printed. This breaks the sub-verse scope rules.
findings.fix: In both files, set source="urn:x-opensiddur:text:bible:ezekiel/3/12/b". Keep the local corresp quoted_ezekiel_3_12. The EN seg may keep the /b reference; a translation that lacks half-verses resolves to the whole verse with a logged warning. Then run validate_urn_references.

findings.problem: The quotation starts at קָדוֹשׁ and leaves out וְקָרָא זֶה אֶל־זֶה וְאָמַר. It also runs past the etnachta on צְבָאוֹת, so neither /a nor /b fits. A whole-verse source over-claims.
findings.fix: Point source at a verse-part that starts at קדוש, e.g. urn:x-opensiddur:text:bible:isaiah/6/3/qadosh. A verse-part runs to the end of the verse, and a half-verse milestone does not end it. Check that opensiddur/common/subverse.py already declares isaiah/6/3/qadosh, which Kedushah needs; if not, declare it there. Apply the same source in both files.

findings.location: Bundle line 71 (HE) and line 356 (EN): second quotation, tei:seg source="urn:x-opensiddur:text:bible:psalms/92/2" (טוֹב לְהֹדוֹת לַייָ / "it is good to thank the Lord.")
findings.problem: Only the first half of Psalms 92:2 is quoted, up to the etnachta on לַיהוָה. וּלְזַמֵּר לְשִׁמְךָ עֶלְיוֹן is not printed. The verse has no ole-we-yored, so the accentual half-verse applies.
findings.fix: In both files, set source="urn:x-opensiddur:text:bible:psalms/92/2/a". The local corresp quoted_psalms_92_2 can stay.

findings.location: Lines 1509–1511: bare j:transclude of prayer:yotzer_or/hakol_yodukha, poem:el_adon and prayer:yotzer_or/lael_asher_shavat. Compare section_yotzer_weekday at lines 1492–1508.
findings.problem: The weekday block is wrapped in a labelled conditional (ביום חול / On a weekday). The Shabbat block is not wrapped at all. When Shabbat is undefined, only Hakol Yodukha carries a rubric (its own "אם שבת" plus a closing delimiter). El Adon and La-El Asher Shavat sit in self-gated conditionals with no instruction, so they print with no delimiters and look unconditional. The Shabbat alternative breaks into three differently marked pieces, and the sequence is not symmetrical.
findings.fix: Wrap lines 1509–1511 in a tei:div xml:id="section_yotzer_shabbat". Give it a j:conditional whose instruction note reads (he) אם שבת and (en) On the Sabbath, testing holiday-aggregate shabbat=true, and put a j:declare of shabbat=true inside it. The declaration settles the files' own Shabbat conditions inside the block, so Hakol Yodukha's own rubric is not printed twice.

findings.problem: This running-order conditional sets shabbat to a single value (false) but declares nothing inside it. Other gated sections in the index, such as section_maariv_veshamru and section_morning_qorbanot_shabbat, include a j:declare. The guideline says to declare the fixed value so that the section's own conditions are settled.
findings.fix: Add a j:declare xml:id="section_yotzer_weekday_settings" with holiday-aggregate shabbat=false around the two transclusions, closed by a matching j:endDeclare.

findings.file: All HE and EN files in scope that quote a verse inside a prayer (morning_numbers_14_17, morning_psalm_25_6, morning_barekhu, lael_asher_shavat, yotzer_qadosh, yotzer_barukh_kevod, yotzer_lael_barukh)
findings.location: For example, bundle line 146: tei:milestone unit="verse" corresp="urn:x-opensiddur:text:siddur:rosh_hashanah/morning_numbers_14_17/1" n="17"
findings.problem: Under Versification, a unit="verse" milestone must carry a canonical bible URN. These carry local siddur/prayer URNs; the canonical identity is only in seg/@source. Avoiding a second copy of a canonical URN is correct, but the unit name implies a canonical verse. This pattern appears to be project-wide.
findings.fix: If the project has no ruling on this yet, use a non-canonical unit for these local quotation anchors (e.g. unit="quotation"), or keep the convention and document it in the project README. Either way, apply it the same way in HE and EN. Optionally rename the local URN suffix .../morning_numbers_14_17/1 and .../morning_psalm_25_6/1 to the quoted_<book>_<ch>_<v> pattern used elsewhere.

findings.location: Bundle line 251 (HE) and line 531 (EN): tei:milestone unit="verse" corresp="urn:x-opensiddur:text:bible:psalms/104/24"
findings.problem: This is the only quotation inside a prayer in scope that uses the canonical bible URN as its corresp. Every sibling quotation uses a local quoted_* URN. It is valid only if Psalms 104:24 appears nowhere else in either project; if it does, only one copy can be reached by that URN.
findings.fix: Confirm Psalms 104:24 is unique in both projects. If it is not, or if you want the files consistent, change the corresp to urn:x-opensiddur:text:prayer:yotzer_or/hameir/quoted_psalms_104_24 in both files and keep source="…psalms/104/24".

findings.file: HE and EN lael_asher_shavat, morning_*, yotzer_* files with quotations
findings.location: Pairs such as tei:milestone unit="chapter" n="92"/ … tei:milestone unit="chapter"/, repeated for each verse (bundle lines 71 and 356)
findings.problem: A chapter milestone with no corresp is a terminator under rule 3, even when it has n. It opens nothing, so these pairs are purely for display and are redundant. In lael_asher_shavat the chapter is closed and reopened between two verses of the same chapter.
findings.fix: Optional: remove the bare chapter pairs, or use one per quotation group. This does not change resolution.

findings.location: Trailing double spaces, e.g. after וּמַמְלִיכִים (bundle line 292), after מְשַׁבֵּחַ וְאוֹמֵר (line 71) and after the el_adon stanzas
findings.problem: Uneven whitespace before milestones and at the end of paragraphs.
findings.fix: Optional: normalize to a single space.

verified: HE and EN share the same correspondences, unit by unit: ahavah_rabbah (div plus prayer-parts ahavah and vahavienu, closed by a terminator), melekh_azur_gevurah stanzas 1–26, el_adon stanzas 1–6, khevodo_ihel stanzas 1–6, morning_barekhu call/response/yitbarakh plus quoted_psalms_113_2, morning_kaddish yitgaddal/yehe_shemeh/yitbarakh, and the div-level URNs for the other yotzer components, or_olam_beotzar_chayyim and yishtabbach. Every milestone sequence that needs a terminator has one.

All five human decisions are reflected in the XML: (1) the melekh_azur_gevurah commentary text, as a standOff note targeting the poem; (2) תִחֵת in stanza 24 and תָּר in stanza 25; (3) אִהֵל in khevodo_ihel/1; (4) the Isaiah 6:3 accents darga and tevir on dalet, merkha on the second yod, etnachta on alef, merkha on lamed, tipcha on alef, siluk on dalet, and a paseq after the first קדוש; (5) קַנֹּא קִנֵּא גָּאֹה גָאָה. The canonical Ofan URN poem:khevodo_ihel is used in both languages and in the index.

Scope checked against the canonical verses, as written in the source: Numbers 14:17, Psalms 25:6, Psalms 113:2, Psalms 104:24, Psalms 136:7 and Psalms 92:1 are whole verses and correctly cited as whole verses.

Notes and descriptions: the source citations (the melekh_azur_gevurah author/acrostic note, אופן. ע״ס א״ב., and וי״א קשוב קול זכירה מזוכרי) are tei:standOff type="notes" commentary. The וי״א note has j:condition as its first child. Speaker rubrics (ח׳, קו״ח, פֿאָרבעטער:, געמיינדע:, Reader:, Congregation:, חזן) are type="description" with role instruction URNs. The condition rubrics (אַם שַׁבָּת. / On the Sabbath. on hakol_yodukha, אם שבת on khevodo) are the conditional's own tei:note type="instruction". "The Reader says half Kaddish." is a description placed after the minyan conditional.

Marked variants in khevodo_ihel stanza 5 behave correctly. HE segment_18 (weekday, no rubric, no type) prints bare when undefined. HE segment_19 and EN segment_6 are type="marked" and match the printed parentheses: when Shabbat is undefined they print in brackets, with the HE instruction אם שבת; when true they print without brackets; when false they are omitted. Descriptions inside the conditioned scope come and go with it.

The minyan conditionals on morning_numbers_14_17, morning_psalm_25_6, morning_kaddish and morning_barekhu have no instruction and no type, so they are processor directions, as the running-order rule requires.

Page references: every tei:pb has ed="1965" and the printed page in n (34–41), and facs follows the scan scheme consistently (HE n95–n109 = scans 96–110, EN n96–n110). The weekday stream (hameir pb 37 and 38) and the Shabbat stream (hakol_yodukha pb 37, el_adon pb 38) each carry their own page breaks, so page navigation still works whichever stream survives. Page numbers are not reused as corresp.

Expanded sequence at index.xml lines 1480–1520: Yishtabbach → Numbers 14:17 → Psalms 25:6 → half Kaddish → Barekhu → Yotzer opening → Or Olam → Melekh Azur Gevurah → weekday (hameir, el_barukh) → Hakol Yodukha → El Adon → La-El Asher Shavat → Titbarakh → Et Shem → Qadosh → Kevodo Ihel → Veha-ofannim → Barukh Kevod → La-El Barukh → Or Chadash → Ahavah Rabbah. Every unit from scans 96–109 appears once, in source order, by canonical URN.
There is no rite-specific text and no opensiddur:rite condition in scans 96–109, so this range has no edition-rite question.
limits: This review does not accept source wording, vocalization, punctuation, sic/corr choices (EN "Name."→"Name," and "prophesy"→"prophecy"), language tags on rubrics, or citation text; those belong to the separate image review.

I had only a file reader, with no search or validator, so I did not run the schema, refdb, validate_urn_references or validate_versification. I could not confirm against the registry or subverse.py that isaiah/6/3/qadosh is declared, or that Psalms 104:24 is unique in either project.
The bundle has bodies and standOff only, no headers. The standOff blocks appear before tei:text in the bundle; I assume that is extraction order and did not check the order inside the actual files.

The dossier's documentary_instructions (s102 "אם שבת ווירד דאס אונטענשטעהענדע הכל יודוך געבעטעט" and s103 "On the Sabbath הכל יודוך which is printed below, is said here") are not in any bundled file. I did not inspect the source projects' own index.xml running order, so I could not check how, or whether, those directives and any page reference are encoded there.

I inspected the expanded index only around the morning sequence (lines 1–150, 700–1000 and 1380–2000). Outside this scope, I noticed that the index uses inconsistent rite feature names (frankfurt at line 982, frankfurt_am_main at lines 1625 and 1949); this needs a separate review.
